summary: Jacqueline Suthren Hirst is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who completed doctoral studies under Julius Lipner. She has held posts at the University of Manchester, including as an Honorary Research Fellow (attested 2026).

Jacques André (1910–1994) was a scholar in linguistics and history and archaeology. He studied at the Faculty of Arts of Paris (~1940–1948) and held posts at Aix-Marseille University (1947–1953), the École Pratique des Hautes Études (1953–1978), and Paris Nanterre University (1965–1970).

Jacques Bacot (1877–1965) was a Tibetologist and linguist who studied under Sylvain Lévi and Paul Pelliot in 1908. He held teaching posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (1919–1938), the University of Paris (~1936–1958), and served as president of the Société Asiatique (1945–1954).

Jacques Gernet (1921–2018) was a sinologist, historian, and Buddhist studies scholar. Educated at Algiers, INALCO, and EPHE, he held chairs and positions at EPHE/EHESS (1955–1976), the University of Paris (from 1957), Paris Diderot University (~1969–1973), and the Collège de France (1975–1992).

Jacques Giès (1950–2021) specialized in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He earned a doctorate from Paris-Sorbonne University under Flora Blanchon, taught at Paris-Sorbonne (1974–1998) and the École du Louvre (1998–2008), and served as president of the Musée Guimet (2008–2011).

Jacques Leider (born 1962) specializes in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He earned degrees from INALCO—including a PhD under Denise Bernot—and Paris-Sorbonne University, later teaching at Chulalongkorn University (1995–1999) before joining the École française d'Extrême-Orient in 2001.

Jacques May (1927–2018) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He served as editor-in-chief of Hōbōgirin (~1964–1981) and as a professor at the University of Lausanne (~1974–1992).

Jacques Scheuer (1942–2021) was an Indologist and scholar of religious studies who studied under Madeleine Biardeau and attended Sorbonne Nouvelle and Université catholique de Louvain. He held academic posts at Université catholique de Louvain (~1978–2007), Centre Sèvres, and KU Leuven (attested 2013).

Jacques Soustelle (1912–1990) was an anthropologist and historian who studied at the École Normale Supérieure and under Marcel Mauss. He held appointments at the Musée de l'Homme, Collège de France, École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1951–1962), and EHESS (~1969–1985).

Jadunath Sarkar (1870–1958) was a historian educated at Presidency University and the University of Calcutta. He held teaching posts at Patna College (1899–1926) and Ravenshaw University, and served as dean of history at Banaras Hindu University (1917–1919) and vice-chancellor of Calcutta University (1926–1928).

Jagdish Kashyap (1908–1976) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar educated at Banaras Hindu University and Vidyalankara Pirivena under Rahul Sankrityayan. He taught Pali at Banaras Hindu University (~1940–1949), Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1959–1965), and directed Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (~1951–1973).

Jaideva Singh (1893–1986) was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under Lakshman Joo and Nankoo Bhaya Telang. He served as chief producer at All India Radio (~1956–1962) and chairman of the Uttar Pradesh Sangeet Natak Akademi (1973).

Jake H. Davis is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who earned an MA at the University of Hawaiʻi and a PhD from CUNY Graduate Center. He has held teaching posts at Brown University, City College of New York, and NYU.

Jakob Steiner (1796–1863) studied at Heidelberg University (1818–1821) and the University of Berlin (1822–1824). He held posts at the University of Applied Sciences Berlin (1825–1834) and Frederick William University Berlin (1834–1863).

Jakob Wilhelm Hauer (1881–1962) was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at Oxford and the University of Tübingen under Richard von Garbe. He held professorships at the University of Marburg (1925–1927) and the University of Tübingen (1927–1945).

James A. Benn is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. Educated at Cambridge, SOAS, and UCLA under Robert E. Buswell Jr., he held teaching posts at Lewis & Clark College and Arizona State University before becoming a professor at McMaster University.

James A. Matisoff (born 1937) is a linguist, Tibetologist, and Sinologist educated at Harvard University and the University of California, Berkeley, where he earned his PhD. After teaching at Columbia University (1966–1969), he served as a professor at UC Berkeley from 1970 to 2002.
James Adam (1860–1907) was a scholar of philosophy who pursued his studies at the University of Aberdeen (~1876–1880) and Gonville and Caius College (~1880–1884).

James Atkinson (1780–1852) was an Edinburgh-educated scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, and Indological studies. He served as Assistant and Deputy Assay Master at the India Government Mint in Kolkata and was appointed Assistant Persian Professor at Fort William College in 1818.

James B. Apple is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He completed his graduate education, including a PhD, at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, where his doctoral supervisor was John D. Dunne.
